statement: Resolve authenticated identity, session validity, current memberships, candidate contexts, permission projection, configuration version, and shell version before protected content renders.
prohibited: Protected content, route names, counts, or tenant structure appearing before authorization completes.
failure: Render a neutral protected-loading state, then route to sign-in, context selection, denied, or safe recovery.

statement: Keep the selected tenant, organization, and facility visibly identified on every private shell surface.
prohibited: Silent context changes or an unlabeled active context.
failure: Freeze risky actions, show context uncertainty, and require explicit selection.

statement: Require explicit confirmation before a user changes to a materially different tenant or facility context.
prohibited: Inferring context from the last clicked record, search result, or stale cache.
failure: Cancel the switch and preserve the current known context.

statement: On context switch, re-evaluate permissions and invalidate routes, search, recents, pins, badges, drafts, and caches that do not belong to the new context.
prohibited: Carrying protected state across contexts.
failure: Clear incompatible state, refresh projections, and record the failed or completed switch.

statement: Use persona defaults only to select ordering, emphasis, and initial landing after authorization filtering.
prohibited: Treating a persona label as a permission or source of truth.
failure: Use a neutral authorized landing and log configuration drift.

statement: When a user has multiple valid contexts and no safe default, require context selection before private domain content appears.
prohibited: Selecting a context using guesswork or a hidden ranking.
failure: Show a disclosure-minimized context picker.

statement: Separate public, invitation, recovery, and authentication surfaces from the private application shell.
prohibited: Leaking private taxonomy, names, counts, or recent activity on pre-authentication surfaces.
failure: Render the minimal pre-authentication shell only.

statement: Preserve one stable correlation identifier across shell bootstrap, context selection, route resolution, and downstream diagnostic events without storing secrets.
prohibited: Logging tokens, credentials, private message bodies, or unrestricted search text.
failure: Redact the payload and retain only privacy-minimized diagnostics.

statement: Maintain a versioned route registry with stable route ID, owner, path pattern, capability, sensitivity, context requirements, lifecycle status, and deep-link policy.
prohibited: Unregistered routes or duplicate route ownership.
failure: Block publication and open a configuration finding.

statement: Build visible navigation from current route eligibility and permission projection rather than a static role-name menu.
prohibited: Showing a menu item as proof that access is granted.
failure: Hide or disable the item and reauthorize at destination.

statement: Reauthorize every route load, refresh, Back/Forward navigation, bookmark, and deep-link open.
prohibited: Relying solely on prior menu visibility or client-side route guards.
failure: Return a disclosure-safe denied or reauthentication state.

statement: Use a persistent or collapsible rail on suitable desktop and tablet widths, with keyboard-operable groups and deterministic collapse behavior.
prohibited: Hover-only access, unreachable collapsed controls, or loss of current-location indication.
failure: Expand to an accessible fallback and preserve content access.

statement: Use a bounded mobile bottom navigation for highest-frequency authorized destinations and an accessible More destination for the remainder.
prohibited: Overcrowded, horizontally scrolling, or permission-leaking mobile navigation.
failure: Reduce to the approved bounded set and expose the remainder through More.

statement: Keep the current destination, parent group, active context, and unsaved-work state perceivable without relying on color alone.
prohibited: Ambiguous location or color-only active indicators.
failure: Add text, icon, state, and assistive labels.

statement: Generate breadcrumbs from registered route relationships and domain-owned labels, not from raw URLs.
prohibited: Exposing identifiers, inaccessible ancestors, or stale names in breadcrumbs.
failure: Suppress unavailable ancestors and retain a safe current-location label.

statement: Provide predictable Back behavior that respects browser history, modal origin, and context boundaries.
prohibited: A Back action that silently changes tenant context or loses unsaved work.
failure: Warn, preserve the draft where authorized, or route to a safe parent.

statement: Treat deep-link descriptors as non-authoritative pointers that may carry only bounded target and context hints.
prohibited: Embedding permission, secrets, protected names, or permanent authority in a link.
failure: Reject or neutralize the link and require fresh authorization.

statement: Use distinct not-found, denied, unavailable, and failed states internally while minimizing disclosure externally.
prohibited: Confirming the existence of a protected resource through error wording or timing.
failure: Return the appropriate safe state with a permitted recovery action.

statement: Store shell preferences as private actor-scoped configuration and never as a source of access.
prohibited: Shared preferences that expose another user’s activity or override policy.
failure: Reset to approved defaults and record a privacy finding.

statement: Reauthorize recents, pins, favorites, and saved views every time they are read or opened.
prohibited: Continuing visibility after relationship, role, context, or permission loss.
failure: Suppress the item and invalidate its display metadata.

statement: Store saved views as filter, sort, column, and presentation definitions without storing protected result rows.
prohibited: Persisting a private dataset inside a view configuration.
failure: Strip result data and require regeneration under current authority.

statement: Allow tenant administrators to configure only an approved allowlist of labels, ordering, group visibility, and defaults.
prohibited: Renaming authoritative domain concepts, hiding mandatory safety routes, or granting access through configuration.
failure: Reject the configuration and keep the last valid version.

statement: Provide a reset-to-default action for user shell preferences without deleting domain records.
prohibited: A preference reset that alters tasks, horse records, billing, or communication state.
failure: Abort and isolate the preference operation.

statement: Expire or trim private recents according to classification, age, and user controls.
prohibited: Indefinite retention of sensitive browsing history by default.
failure: Remove expired pointers and preserve only required audit evidence.

statement: Keep badge counts and summaries minimum-necessary and independently revalidated.
prohibited: Showing protected names, health details, financial amounts, safeguarding facts, or stale counts in the shell.
failure: Replace with a generic authorized indicator or suppress the badge.

statement: Do not use behavioral advertising, unrelated profiling, or manipulative engagement ranking in shell personalization.
prohibited: Cross-context tracking, dark patterns, or personalization aimed at minors.
failure: Disable the feature, preserve evidence, and open a governance finding.

statement: Treat search as an authorized view of existing source truth and never as a source of ownership, custody, consent, relationship, professional authority, financial responsibility, or permission.
prohibited: Creating authority or factual truth from a result, rank, suggestion, or index entry.
failure: Display source context and require the authoritative workflow for consequential action.

statement: Scope global search to the current actor and active context unless a separately approved discovery mode explicitly narrows and explains another scope.
prohibited: Identifiable cross-tenant search by default.
failure: Return no cross-tenant result and record prohibited enumeration attempts.

statement: Apply permission and classification filtering before retrieval where technically possible and again before presentation and open.
prohibited: Relying on post-render masking or client-only filtering.
failure: Suppress the result and invalidate the affected index projection.

statement: Exclude safeguarding records, precise location, private communications, credentials, secrets, raw financial identifiers, and other protected fields from general search.
prohibited: Indexing protected content into ordinary global search.
failure: Remove the fields, reindex, assess exposure, and preserve incident evidence.

statement: Apply heightened protections to minors, guardianship, location, contact, and recommendation results.
prohibited: Open-ended minor directories, contact discovery, or behavioral recommendation.
failure: Suppress, narrow, and route to a specialized authorized workflow.

statement: Keep autocomplete and suggestions permission-bound, minimum-necessary, context-aware, and resistant to enumeration.
prohibited: Revealing inaccessible names or record existence through prefix probing.
failure: Rate-limit, suppress, and emit an abuse signal.

statement: Label result type, authoritative source, current context, freshness, and meaningful limitation where needed for safe interpretation.
prohibited: Presenting stale or derived data as current authoritative truth.
failure: Mark stale, restrict action, or route to refresh.

statement: Use neutral, explainable ranking based on relevance, recency, domain priority, and user-selected filters.
prohibited: Paid placement, secret favoritism, or ranking that changes authority.
failure: Fall back to deterministic neutral ordering and record the configuration defect.

statement: Propagate correction, revocation, restriction, deletion, and relationship changes into indexes, suggestions, caches, and result snippets within defined service bounds.
prohibited: Continuing to surface withdrawn or unauthorized information.
failure: Suppress immediately where possible, queue repair, and expose freshness status.

statement: Minimize ordinary query history and provide proportionate user controls; apply heightened logging only to defined high-risk or privileged searches.
prohibited: Indefinite full-text query retention or hidden privileged browsing.
failure: Redact, shorten retention, and require privileged-search review.

statement: Detect and respond to scraping, harvesting, stalking, enumeration, bulk export patterns, and location probing.
prohibited: Unbounded automated discovery or silent bulk extraction.
failure: Throttle, block, challenge, alert, and preserve privacy-minimized evidence.

statement: Keep semantic or AI-assisted retrieval default OFF until separately authorized with source attribution, tenant isolation, permission filtering, evaluation, disablement, and provider controls.
prohibited: Connecting customer data to an unapproved model or shared training corpus.
failure: Disable the feature and remove generated or indexed derivatives.

statement: Register every command with stable ID, owner, display rule, input schema, execution endpoint, risk level, authorization rule, and evidence rule.
prohibited: Free-form executable commands or commands without a domain owner.
failure: Do not publish the command.

statement: Separate command discovery authorization from execution-time authorization and re-evaluate immediately before execution.
prohibited: Executing because the command was visible earlier.
failure: Deny, explain safely, and refresh the command list.

statement: Require confirmation, recent authentication, step-up, or dual control for commands classified as consequential.
prohibited: One-click execution of high-risk financial, safeguarding, access, or deletion actions.
failure: Hold the request pending the required control.

statement: Use idempotency keys and explicit pending, completed, failed, canceled, and reconciled states for effectful quick actions.
prohibited: Duplicate effects caused by retry, refresh, or double activation.
failure: Return the prior result or place the action into reconciliation.

statement: Limit Quick Create to registered domain-owned forms and current create authority in the active context.
prohibited: A generic shell form that invents domain rules or creates in the wrong tenant.
failure: Block launch and direct to context correction.

statement: Preserve unsaved quick-action input only within authorized context and classification limits.
prohibited: Carrying a protected draft across users, contexts, or expired sessions.
failure: Clear or securely quarantine the draft.

statement: Keep shell commands keyboard accessible, searchable without disclosure, and operable without pointer-only interaction.
prohibited: Mouse-only, hover-only, or unannounced command behavior.
failure: Expose an accessible alternative and suppress unsupported shortcuts.

statement: Never let a shell command bypass the domain workflow, validation, audit, consent, or approval requirements owned by another PIA.
prohibited: Treating shell convenience as substantive authority.
failure: Route to the domain-owned workflow and preserve the attempted shortcut evidence.

statement: Provide deterministic loading, ready, empty, denied, unavailable, degraded, stale, conflict, and error states for every shell surface.
prohibited: Blank screens, misleading success, or one generic state for materially different conditions.
failure: Render the safe state and a permitted recovery path.

statement: Prevent protected-content flash during bootstrap, context change, session expiry, route transition, and cache restore.
prohibited: Showing prior authorized content before current authorization resolves.
failure: Mask protected regions until resolution.

statement: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA for web and equivalent native-platform accessibility expectations, including keyboard, focus, names, roles, reflow, zoom, text scaling, and reduced motion.
prohibited: Color-only meaning, hidden focus, inaccessible modal traps, or essential image-only text.
failure: Block release or disable the affected presentation.

statement: Use at least 44 by 44 CSS pixel or point targets for primary field actions unless an equivalent accessible pattern is documented and tested.
prohibited: Tiny high-frequency controls unsuitable for barn conditions.
failure: Use a larger control or alternate action surface.

statement: Preserve critical actions in glare, gloves, one-handed use, intermittent connectivity, and small-screen conditions.
prohibited: Precision-only gestures or low-contrast operational controls.
failure: Expose a simplified text-first fallback.

statement: Keep serious workflows free from celebratory animation, playful copy, mascot treatment, or decorative typography that could trivialize risk.
prohibited: Stead or decorative celebration during injury, medication, safeguarding, payment approval, security, legal, or outage workflows.
failure: Suppress decoration and render a neutral serious-workflow state.

statement: Incorporate the approved visual-system V0.3.1 by exact source bytes and SHA-256 without editing its approved content.
prohibited: Recreating, rewriting, or silently superseding the approved component inside this candidate.
failure: Stop package assembly and obtain the verified exact source file.

statement: Apply the approved visual hierarchy, typography roles, color separation, icon system, and Stead restrictions only within the scope and conditions recorded by V0.3.1.
prohibited: Extending visual approval into product behavior or activating Stead without separate authority.
failure: Use neutral shell defaults and open a design deviation.

statement: Cache only explicitly approved shell metadata and authorized minimum-necessary pointers with tenant, actor, version, expiry, classification, and revocation watermark.
prohibited: Caching unrestricted search results, protected snippets, secrets, or cross-tenant state.
failure: Purge the cache and assess exposure.

statement: Display persistent offline, stale, queued, failed, and synchronization-conflict status without implying server confirmation.
prohibited: Silent local success or hiding stale authority.
failure: Keep the action pending or blocked and explain next safe step.

statement: Do not treat cached route visibility, prior search results, badges, or context as continuing authority.
prohibited: Opening protected content solely because it was previously cached.
failure: Restrict to approved offline projection or require reconnection.

statement: On reconnect, refresh identity, session, context, permissions, route registry, configuration, revocation watermark, and affected cached pointers before privileged actions.
prohibited: Replaying stale actions before authority refresh.
failure: Hold the queue and reconcile each action.

statement: Bind queued shell actions to actor, device, tenant, facility, command version, idempotency key, and creation time.
prohibited: Replaying an action in a different context or under a different user.
failure: Reject and preserve a reconciliation record.

statement: Support secure device sign-out, session revocation, and cache purge with a documented limitation when the device remains unreachable.
prohibited: Claiming immediate remote deletion when it cannot be proven.
failure: Revoke server authority, mark purge pending, and communicate the limitation.

statement: Use least privilege and field-level projection for shell bootstrap, navigation, search, badges, recents, support, and diagnostics.
prohibited: A broad administrator label granting universal shell visibility.
failure: Deny the projection and require action-specific authority.

statement: Require support mode to be separately authorized, purpose-bound, time-limited, visibly indicated, attributable, and fully auditable.
prohibited: Hidden impersonation, unrestricted browsing, or support access without a valid target and purpose.
failure: Block or terminate the support session and alert.

statement: Minimize telemetry and diagnostics and prohibit secrets, credentials, unrestricted queries, message bodies, sensitive health detail, and safeguarding content in ordinary logs.
prohibited: Using observability as a shadow data store.
failure: Redact, rotate, investigate, and correct instrumentation.

statement: Apply safeguarding restrictions across route visibility, search, suggestions, notifications, badges, recents, exports, support, and caches.
prohibited: A general shell feature bypassing a protective restriction.
failure: Suppress access, invalidate derived state, and escalate under the safeguarding process.

statement: Expose a versioned shell-bootstrap contract with explicit context candidates, authorized capabilities, route version, configuration version, freshness, and safe failure codes.
prohibited: Returning full domain datasets or ambiguous authorization state in bootstrap.
failure: Return a minimal safe response and require recovery.

statement: Use versioned search, command, preference, recents, notification-summary, support-session, and configuration contracts with schema validation and backwards-compatibility rules.
prohibited: Ad hoc unversioned payloads or silent field reinterpretation.
failure: Reject incompatible requests and retain the prior supported contract.

statement: Publish attributable events for context changes, privileged searches, consequential commands, support sessions, configuration publication, and route lifecycle changes.
prohibited: Relying solely on client analytics for consequential evidence.
failure: Fail closed where evidence is mandatory or queue an auditable event.

statement: Run index repair, revocation propagation, cache expiry, badge refresh, saved-view cleanup, and configuration validation as bounded idempotent jobs with observable outcomes.
prohibited: Unbounded jobs, duplicate effects, or silent partial completion.
failure: Pause, retry safely, reconcile, and alert.

statement: Scope feature flags by environment, tenant, cohort, capability, and version with safe defaults, named owner, expiry, and emergency disablement.
prohibited: A flag that grants authority, stores secrets, or remains indefinitely without owner.
failure: Use the safe default and block publication.

statement: Keep secrets, signing keys, provider credentials, and private tokens outside source, client bundles, PIA artifacts, screenshots, logs, and configuration payloads.
prohibited: Embedding or documenting live secrets in the shell package.
failure: Revoke, rotate, redact, and treat as a security incident.

statement: Inventory current routes, menus, labels, deep links, role-based shortcuts, search fields, caches, preferences, and legacy shell assets before migration.
prohibited: Replacing the shell without a reconciliation map or historical evidence.
failure: Stop migration and complete the inventory.

statement: Roll out shell changes through controlled environments and cohorts with preflight validation, telemetry, stop conditions, rollback, and post-release verification.
prohibited: All-at-once activation without tested rollback.
failure: Stop rollout and restore the last verified configuration or build.

statement: Decommission routes, commands, search fields, and assets by removing active exposure, migrating lawful preferences/links, invalidating caches, and preserving history.
prohibited: Deleting history or leaving a retired entry point active.
failure: Quarantine the route and complete decommission evidence.

statement: Provide operational dashboards for bootstrap failures, route denials, context-switch defects, search latency/errors, stale indexes, abuse signals, support sessions, job failures, and configuration drift.
prohibited: Metrics that expose protected content or falsely imply operational readiness.
failure: Use privacy-minimized aggregates and mark evidence state accurately.

statement: Provide bounded administrative tools for route/configuration validation, cache invalidation, index repair, support-session termination, and feature disablement.
prohibited: Direct database editing or unrestricted production browsing as the standard support path.
failure: Disable the unsafe tool and use a controlled procedure.

statement: Reconcile the as-built shell to every applicable requirement, source, decision, route, contract, test, evidence item, and incorporated visual-system hash before verification.
prohibited: Claiming conformance from screenshots, demos, or unexecuted tests.
failure: Classify drift and block verification until resolved or formally accepted.
